newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia offshore debt issue remains option.
newsitem.headline: Australia offshore debt issue remains option.

text.p: The Australian Treasury said on Wednesday a return to direct debt issuance in offshore markets remained an option if this was assessed as advantageous.

"(However) this should not be taken as foreshadowing an imminent offshore borrowing by the Commonwealth," Tony Hinton, First Assistant Secretary, Investment and Debt Division Commowealth Treasury, said in an address to the Australian Financial Markets Association (AFMA) in Sydney.
Hinton said that if there was a return to issuance offshore, there would be a corresponding reduction in the domestic issuance programme.

Hinton said that for a number of years a strategy of obtaining desired new foreign currency exposure through issuing domestically and swapping the proceeds had been employed as this had offered cost advantages over the alternative of direct public offshore issuance.
"Narrower Australian dollar swap spreads mean that currently the cost advantage of issuing domestically and swapping is relatively small, particularly at shorter maturities," he said.

The practice of recent years of maintaining a small core holding of U.S. dollar debt in the portfolio would continue in 1996/97 (to June 30), involving the acquisition of new exposure of around A$3.0 billion after allowance for scheduled maturities, Hinton added.
